description: Weekly, grouped, conservative — CI decides (typecheck, unit tests, smoke on the built bundle, pixel comparison, size budget, site build). The reasoning is in docs/09-engineering-notes.md §10.

schedule: on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: one PR a week for everything minor and patch
majors wait in the Dependency Dashboard until someone ticks them — an open major would otherwise hold one of the five branch slots for weeks
dev-only patch updates merge themselves once CI is green
what ships in the bundle or the npm package is merged by hand
prBodyNotes: These land in the published bundle (`map0-viewer`). Check the page-tier line of `pnpm size` in the CI log, and the smoke and visual steps.

packageRules.description: a peer range widens on a major instead of leaving older consumers behind
MapLibre: three copied files and a worker, and an optional peer of the published package (docs/09 §3.1)
prBodyNotes: MapLibre is copied into dist as three files (docs/09 §3.1) and is an optional peer of `map0-viewer`. On a major, run `pnpm build:npm && node e2e/verify-types.mjs` as well.

packageRules.description: a new Playwright is a new Chromium build, and that changes pixels
prBodyNotes: The visual step stays red until the baselines are refreshed: `pnpm build && pnpm visual:linux --update` (Docker) and `pnpm visual --update`, then look at every rewritten PNG under e2e/visual/ and commit them to this branch.

packageRules.description: pnpm itself (the packageManager field): a minor can change the lockfile
Node in the workflows (node-version): new LTS majors only, never pinned or bumped to a patch release. By depName: setup-node's packageName is actions/node-versions
engines.node says which Node a user may run, so it moves by hand, never with a release
@types/node follows the oldest Node map0-check supports (engines.node >=22), not the newest
